# Tasks — Feature Plan (v1.0 DSL Specification) Markdown-native task management for filemark. **Reader-first.** Markdown is the source of truth, AI writes, filemark visualizes. Same story as datagrid / chart / kanban / stats / ADR — one structured shape, many views — now applied to tasks. This doc is the canonical spec for the DSL and the component surface. It survives every parser rewrite. Lock it before writing code; update it when shipping. - **Date opened:** 2026-04-24 - **Package:** `@filemark/tasks` (shipped 2026-04-24) - **Host integration:** `@filemark/mdx` (parser, context, `` / `` / `` components shipped). `` lives in `@filemark/mdx` rather than extending `@filemark/kanban` — simpler, no cross-package coupling. `apps/chrome-ext` (cross-file `` + `useTaskIndex` + ⌘T shortcut + TopBar toggle shipped; CLI deferred to Phase 6). - **Follow-on doc:** `docsi/TASKS_MD.md` (technical reference, written post-ship; copies finalized sections from this plan) --- ## Shipping status (updated 2026-04-24) **Phases 1–5 live. Phase 6 explicitly SKIPPED** — out of scope for current v1.0 use. Revisit if/when a concrete use case arrives. | Phase | Scope | Status | |---|---|---| | **1** | Parser, types, round-trip serializer, TasksContext, enhanced `
  • ` TaskItem with chips | ✅ **shipped** | | **2** | Predicate DSL (`filterTasks` / `parseFilter`), `groupTasks` / `sortTasks`, `` with filter/group-by/sort/limit/order, frontmatter defaults cascade | ✅ **shipped** | | **3** | `` built on ``, `` (KanbanFromTasks) with group-by/filter/order/height, typed-shortcode link chips + URL auto-detection | ✅ **shipped** | | **4** | Cross-file task panel (`useTaskIndex` store, ``, ⌘T toggle, filter tabs + search + group chooser, click-to-open with scroll-to-line flash), `data-fv-task-line` anchor on task rows, UIPrefs persistence | ✅ **shipped** (CLI deferred to Phase 6 = skipped) | | **5** | Recurrence layer (`every:` parsing + chip + `is:recurring` predicate), `resolveBlockers` for dependency-aware `is:blocked` / `is:unblocked` + "🚧 blocked by N" chip, `` SVG Gantt-lite | ✅ **shipped** (Calendar deferred to Phase 6 = skipped) | | **6** | LSP, formal `grammar.pegjs`, Shiki language def, import/export adapters (Obsidian Tasks / Logseq / Todo.txt / iCal / JSON-LD), AI `@ai:` action markers, `filemark tasks ` CLI, `` | ⏸ **SKIP** — out of scope; too advanced for current needs. No plans to build unless a specific use case pulls on it. | ### Small Phase 1–5 items still open (non-blocking) These are minor gaps inside shipped phases. None block current use. Listed so they're not forgotten, not scheduled. - **`{k:v}` dense-metadata block parsing** (Phase 1 grammar §5.5) — `- [ ] Ship v2 {owner: alice, priority: p0}` syntax. Never shipped. Sigil form handles all practical cases; block form is YAGNI for now. - **`` fenced-block renderer** (Phase 2) — rendering `` ```tasks `` fences as their own list/board/stats views. Deferred; the `` + inline bullets workaround handles this. - **Grammar-version dispatcher** (Phase 1) — parser currently ignores `tasks-version:` in frontmatter. Declaration accepted, not enforced. Wire up only when we actually have a v1.1 with different semantics. - **``** — month-grid view. Deferred; Timeline + Stats cover "when does work land" at our scale. - **`filemark tasks ` CLI** — grep / show / format / export / stats / graph / lint / validate. Deferred; the interactive TaskPanel + shell `grep -r` cover the use cases. **What's actually live right now (2026-04-24):** - Every `- [ ]` bullet in any rendered markdown doc gets enhanced automatically — 6 statuses, 14 sigils (including `every:` for recurrence), metadata chips inline. - ``, ``, ``, `` tag handlers wired into `MDXViewer`. - **Cross-file ``** — toggled by `⌘T` or the list-todo icon in the TopBar. Aggregates tasks from every opened markdown file; filter tabs (All · Open · Today · This week · Overdue · Blocked); search; group-by (status / owner / priority / project / file / due-bucket / tag / flat); click-to-open jumps the viewer to the source line with a transient flash. - **`useTaskIndex` store** in `apps/chrome-ext/src/app/taskIndex.ts` — content-hash-keyed cache of `Task[]` per file; `indexFile` is called from Viewer on every content change; dedupes repeated calls with unchanged bytes. - **Recurrence + dependency resolution** — `every:daily` and friends parse + render; `resolveBlockers` walks the graph so `is:blocked` / `is:unblocked` correctly reflect prerequisite status; "🚧 blocked by N" chip on tasks with unresolved prereqs. - **``** — SVG date-axis Gantt-lite grouped by lane; bars for `^start..~due`, diamond markers for due-only, open-ended arrows for start-only; today vertical dashed marker; priority colors. - Demo doc `examples/tasks-full.md` with 30 showcase sections exercising every layer. - Playground gallery entry under "Planning" section (note: playground doesn't have the TaskPanel — that's a chrome-ext-only feature since it needs multi-file library state). - Round-trip `parseTaskLine → serializeTask → parseTaskLine` is byte-stable for canonical inputs (including `every:`). **Known gotchas surfaced during the build — see §19 Authoring caveats below.** --- ## Positioning — why anyone would use this ### The one-liner **Your markdown is the database. Filemark is the lens.** Tasks live where your plans, specs, and brainstorms live — same folder, same files, same grep, same AI context. No separate app, no DB, no server, no lock-in. ### The problem every knowledge worker has Brainstorms, plans, and specs are written in markdown (because nothing else is as flexible). But the *tasks inside those documents* live somewhere else — Notion, Linear, Todoist, Jira, Asana, Things, Apple Reminders, a sticky note. Three bad consequences: 1. **Context loss.** The task says "Ship datagrid v2" — but the *why*, the *design*, the *tradeoffs* live in a markdown doc 3 tabs away. Reading the task doesn't give you the plan it belongs to. 2. **Fork and forget.** You copy the task into Linear. The markdown plan evolves. The Linear issue goes stale. Now you have two sources of truth and neither is current. 3. **Grep breaks.** Your brain wants one answer to "show me everything about the launch." Markdown answers that (one folder, one grep). Fragmented tools don't. ### What filemark does differently Every rival solves "task management" by **owning the data** (DB, SaaS, proprietary format). Filemark owns none of it. Your tasks are `- [ ] …` lines in the same markdown files you already write in. Filemark is a rendering layer — not a backend. ### Seven reasons this wins for the right user 1. **Source of truth is plain files you already edit.** Nothing proprietary. Ten years from now those files still open in `cat`, VS Code, Obsidian, GitHub preview, or whatever replaces them. 2. **Tasks live inside the plan, not next to it.** Read the spec → see the tasks inline where they belong. No context switch to a separate tool. 3. **One `grep` answers everything.** Your entire planning knowledge base is one folder. `grep -r "@alice !p0"` finds every task Alice owns at top priority across every project. A DB-backed tool can't do that without a query layer — and then only within that tool's silo. 4. **AI-native.** Claude (or any LLM) reads + writes markdown fluently. It reads your files directly and edits one line at a time. No API integration layer, no export/import dance, no custom MCP server needed. The workflow is: *"Claude, update the sprint plan — mark datagrid as done and add a timeline task for next Monday."* One markdown edit; filemark re-renders. 5. **Reader-first, not editor lock-in.** Edit in VS Code, Obsidian, nano, on your phone via Working Copy, via Claude, via `sed` — filemark doesn't care. It just visualizes. This is the inverse of Notion / Obsidian / Logseq, all of which want to own the editing surface. 6. **Zero lock-in, zero dependency, zero cost.** No server. No account. No subscription. No data leaves the machine. Delete filemark tomorrow; your tasks are still `- [ ]` bullets in files you own. 7. **Many views, one source.** Same task lines rendered as list, kanban board, KPI cards, (later) timeline, calendar, dashboard. The data never forks. Auto-refresh means every view updates the instant you save. ### Who this is for - **Solo brainstormers** who live in markdown already and want their tasks to live there too - **AI-assisted planners** — people who ask Claude/ChatGPT to draft plans and want those plans rendered richly without copy-paste into another tool - **Spec / RFC / design-doc authors** who want tasks embedded in the document they belong to - **Indie hackers and solo devs** drafting roadmaps in markdown and tracking progress across projects - **Researchers** managing a running list of questions, leads, and follow-ups across many notes - **Developers** who already `grep -r "TODO"` through their repo and want the grep to work the same way for personal plans - **PKM power users** (Obsidian / Logseq / Dendron) who want a richer reader layer over the same markdown files they already maintain ### Who this is NOT for - **Teams needing real-time multi-user collaboration** — use Notion / Linear / GitHub Projects - **Enterprises needing SSO, RBAC, audit logs, compliance** — not a filemark fit - **People who want a backend to guarantee "my tasks are safe in the cloud"** — your markdown folder + git solves that; filemark doesn't try to be a cloud service - **Power users who want tasks managed from a CLI-first workflow** — use Taskwarrior / todo.txt directly; filemark is a reader, not a task CLI (though the `filemark tasks` subcommands are provided for AI tool-use, not primary UX) - **Users who have thousands of tasks per day across millions of records** — at that scale you want a real DB; filemark is designed for ~1000s of items in a personal knowledge base ### The competitive landscape | Tool | Model | Why filemark-tasks is different | |---|---|---| | Notion | SaaS, block-based DB | Proprietary; AI can't edit without API; lock-in | | Linear / Jira / Asana | SaaS team tool | Heavyweight; separated from the plan context | | Todoist / Things | Pure task app | No plan/spec context; separate data silo | | Obsidian Tasks plugin | Editor-first plugin | Powerful but tied to Obsidian; editor lock-in | | Logseq | Editor-first, block-based | Specific data model; not a pure reader | | Dendron | Hierarchical notes + TODO | Editor-first; VS Code-only | | Taskwarrior / todo.txt | CLI-first | No visualization; no plan context | | GitHub Issues | Repo-attached | Public-facing; per-repo, not personal | | Emacs Org-mode | Emacs-native | Editor-locked; steep curve | | Apple Reminders / Google Tasks | OS notification tool | Zero doc context | **The empty quadrant filemark owns:** reader-first + markdown-native + multi-view + AI-editable + zero-lock-in + embedded-in-plans. ### Taglines worth A/B-testing - *"Your markdown is the database."* - *"Tasks where plans live."* - *"AI-native task management. Just files."* - *"Stop copying your plans into a task app. Render them in place."* - *"One folder. Every view. Zero lock-in."* - *"A lens, not a platform."* ### The thirty-second pitch > You write plans, specs, brainstorms in markdown. You always have. Your tasks live inside those docs — `- [ ] build X`, `- [ ] refactor Y`. But your project tracker is somewhere else, so tasks drift out of sync with the plans they came from. > > Filemark is a Chrome extension that renders your existing markdown folder as a rich view — tasks become interactive checkboxes with priority pills, owners, due dates, status columns. Same markdown file. Same grep. Same AI context. Add a ` ```kanban ` fence and the same tasks become a board. Add `` and the same tasks become KPI cards. > > You still edit in whatever editor you like — VS Code, Obsidian, Claude. Filemark never owns your data. It just reads the files you already write. > > No account. No server. No subscription. It's a lens, not a platform. --- ## 1. Goals - **Best-in-class markdown task system that an AI can author, grep, and edit programmatically — and filemark renders beautifully as list / board / stats / timeline.** - **Zero author friction.** A plain `- [ ] text` GFM bullet is already a valid task. All metadata is optional. - **Multiple views over one data source.** List, board, stats, timeline, calendar — all fed by the same parsed `Task[]`. - **Cross-file aggregation.** Side panel walks every opened document and shows a global view. - **Tool-compatible syntax.** Renders fine in GitHub, Obsidian, Logseq, Dendron; those tools just see metadata tokens as literal text instead of chips. - **Reader-first philosophy preserved.** No write-back from inside filemark's markdown rendering. AI edits the file; filemark re-renders on auto-refresh. The existing checkbox persistence (via `StorageAdapter`) is a tracked exception — user-local state only, never lands in the source file. - **Grep-friendly by design.** One task = one line. ASCII sigils. ISO dates. Identifier-safe payloads. A line of shell regex answers most queries without parser involvement. - **AI-friendly by design.** Round-trip parse → serialize is byte-identical. Tail-scan rules are simple enough for an LLM to emit correctly first try. Predicate DSL lets an LLM translate natural-language queries into structured filters. - **Composable DSL.** Nine formal layers (status, identity, metadata, time, references, relationships, recurrence, queries, extensibility) each with its own grammar that composes without ambiguity. --- ## 2. Non-goals (explicit) - **Task editor inside filemark.** We're a reader. The user (or their AI) edits markdown in their editor; filemark picks up the change on auto-refresh. - **Remote sync / accounts / teams.** Local-only. Two people editing the same file is a git merge concern — filemark doesn't arbitrate. - **Task creation UI.** No "Add task" button. Authors write the markdown; that's the feature. - **Deep query language.** A small predicate DSL is enough. No SQL, no GraphQL, no saved-view catalog. - **Recurring task expansion.** We store the RRULE; we don't eagerly enumerate every future instance. - **Sub-task drag-reordering.** Reorder in the editor. - **Multi-line tasks.** One task = one line is a hard invariant for grep-friendliness. Long content goes in a child bullet or sibling prose. - **Quoted string values.** `@"alice smith"` breaks word-boundary regex and grep patterns. Identifiers are `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`. - **Unicode sigils.** Cross-platform regex hell. ASCII only. - **Task write-back from filemark's UI.** Tick state persists via `StorageAdapter` (local); we don't modify the source file. - **Integration with Jira / Linear / GitHub as task SOT.** The markdown file is the canonical surface; exporters/importers bridge to those tools. --- ## 3. Authoring Every task starts as a GFM checkbox bullet. Authors can place tasks inline in prose or inside a `` ```tasks `` fence. Both produce identical `Task` objects and both contribute to the same `TasksContext`. ### 3.1 Inline (in-prose) tasks ```md - [ ] Ship datagrid v2 @alice !p0 ~2026-04-28 #grid (launch) - [/] Refactor auth middleware @grace !p1 ^2026-04-25 ~2026-04-29 #auth - [!] DB migration blocked @linus !p0 #infra - [x] Pick launch logo @karen #design - [?] Kill legacy sparkline? @karen #design - [-] Old mobile prototype @alice #mobile ``` Interactive — each line is rendered by the enhanced `TaskCheckbox` with chips inline. ### 3.2 Fenced tasks block ```md ```tasks id=backlog group-by=status title="Sprint 2 — Backlog" default-owner=alice default-project=launch - [ ] Ship datagrid v2 !p0 ~2026-04-28 #grid - [x] Pick logo @karen #design - [/] Refactor auth @grace !p1 ^2026-04-25 ~2026-04-29 #auth - [!] DB migration blocked @linus !p0 #infra ``` ``` Inside the fence: identical grammar; author can omit fields covered by `default-*` in the info-string. On the fence: info-string flags control authoring defaults and the rendered view. ### 3.3 Info-string flags on the fence | Flag | Default | Notes | |---|---|---| | `id=` | — | Makes the fence referenceable via ``. | | `view=list\|kanban\|stats\|table\|timeline\|calendar` | `list` | What to render. | | `group-by=[,]` | — | One or two-level grouping. | | `filter=` | — | Predicate DSL (§9.1). | | `sort=[:asc\|desc][,…]` | source order | Multi-key sort. | | `limit=` | — | Cap rendered rows. | | `default-owner=` | — | Fills empty `@owner` on each task. | | `default-priority=

    ` | — | Fills empty `!priority`. | | `default-project=` | — | Fills empty `(project)`. | | `title=` | — | Header above the rendered view. | | `src=` | — | External source; relative resolves via AssetResolver, absolute URL fetched, `#id` references another fence. | | `collapsed` | — | Render collapsed by default. | | `tasks-version=` | `1.0` | Grammar version; pinned per fence. | ### 3.4 Frontmatter defaults ```yaml --- title: Sprint 2 project: launch default-owner: alice default-priority: p1 tasks-version: 1.0 --- ``` Defaults cascade: `task-line > fence > frontmatter > filemark-global`. Each explicit value wins; missing values fall through. ### 3.5 Nested subtasks ```md - [ ] Ship datagrid v2 @alice !p0 ~2026-04-28 - [x] Multi-sort - [/] Typed filters - [ ] Aggregation footer ``` Indent ≥ parent + 2 spaces → subtask. Parent's rendered "completion %" is derived from child statuses unless parent is explicitly `[x]` / `[-]`. ### 3.6 Notes / context below a task A task owns the child bullets that aren't also tasks. Use them for context, commentary, research links: ```md - [ ] Ship datagrid v2 @alice !p0 ~2026-04-28 - PR: gh:anthropic/filemark#142 - Blockers: nothing confirmed — design handoff pending - Waiting on Linus to review the group-by path ``` Non-task child bullets become `task.notes[]` in the parse output. --- ## 4. The DSL — nine formal layers A world-class task DSL is nine layered grammars. Each layer has its own formal spec; layers compose without ambiguity because every token has exactly one meaning and every sigil is non-overlapping. ### 4.1 Layer 1 — Status The checkbox character determines status. Six states; ordered; grep-friendly. | Char | Status | Kanban column default | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | ` ` | `todo` | Todo | GFM default | | `/` | `wip` | In Progress | Obsidian/Logseq convention | | `x` / `X` | `done` | Done | GFM default; strikethrough | | `!` | `blocked` | Blocked | Amber alert icon | | `?` | `question` | Needs Decision | Planning docs | | `-` | `cancelled` | (hidden) | Strikethrough; not counted | Reserved for future: `[>]` delegated, `[~]` snoozed, `[=]` waiting — **not v1.0**. If enabled in a later version, behind a `tasks-version` pin. ### 4.2 Layer 2 — Identity Every task has a stable id. Two modes: 1. **Auto-id:** derived `hash(file:line:text)`. Survives edits to the same line; breaks when the line moves or the text changes. 2. **Stable id:** `^task-` suffix on the line. Survives moves, renames, reorders, edits. Format: `^task-[a-z0-9-]+`. Distinct from `^2026-…` (ISO date) because the regex is unambiguous — date-shaped → start-date sigil, identifier-shaped → id sigil. **Auto-promotion.** Formatter (or `` render pass) can promote a task to a stable id the first time it's referenced from another task's `after:` / `parent:` / `blocks:` — preventing orphan references when the source line moves. ### 4.3 Layer 3 — Metadata sigils Each metadata sigil is one ASCII character. Single meaning. Space-delimited. Identifier-safe payload. | Sigil | Field | Type | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | `@alice` | `owners[]` | string | Multiple allowed. Whitespace delimits. | | `!p0` | `priority` | enum | `p0..p3` or `high` / `med` / `low` aliases. | | `~2026-04-28` | `due` | date/keyword | ISO or §4.4 keyword. | | `^2026-04-22` | `start` | date/keyword | Pairs with `~due` for Timeline. | | `#tag` | `tags[]` | string | Supports `#area/work` hierarchy via `/`. | | `(project)` | `project` | string | Single per task. Parenthesized. | | `&2h` | `estimate` | duration | Units: `m`, `h`, `d`, `w`. | | `$500` | `cost` | money | Number + optional ISO currency. | | `%40` | `percent` | 0–100 | Progress override. | | `.area/work` | `area` | path | Dotted notation for life/OKR area. | | `*goal-q2` | `goal` | id ref | Link to a higher-level goal. | | `+2026-04-24` | `created` | date | Auto-filled on first parse. | | `=2026-04-27` | `completed` | date | Auto-filled on first `[x]` transition. | **`x-foo=value`** — Layer 9 (extensibility) custom fields. Shown generic unless a plugin renderer is registered. ### 4.4 Layer 4 — Time expressions (`~` / `^` payloads) Time is first-class, not stringly-typed. Payloads parse into typed intervals. **Absolute:** - ISO date: `2026-04-28` - ISO week: `2026-W17` - ISO month: `2026-04` - ISO quarter: `2026-Q2` **Keywords:** - `today`, `tomorrow`, `yesterday` - `this-week`, `next-week`, `last-week` - `this-month`, `next-month` - `eod` (end of day), `eow` (end of week), `eom`, `eoq`, `eoy` - `monday`, `tuesday`, … (next occurrence) - `next-friday`, `last-monday` **Relative offsets:** - `+1d`, `+2w`, `+3m`, `+1y` (calendar units) - `+5bd` (business days) - `-7d` (past; for `^start` only) **Ranges (for `~due`):** - `~2026-04-28..2026-05-01` (closed range) - `~>=2026-04-28` (open-ended lower) - `~<=eow` (open-ended upper) All computed once at parse time against the browser's local time zone (documented as such in TASKS_MD.md). ### 4.5 Layer 5 — External references Tasks link outward to PRs, issues, design docs, Slack threads. Three complementary forms. **Form A — standard markdown link** ```md - [ ] Ship datagrid v2 [PR #42](https://github.com/org/repo/pull/42) @alice !p0 ``` Parser preserves the inline markdown link as-is in rendered output. Task object gets: ```ts task.links = [{ kind: "url", label: "PR #42", url: "https://…" }]; ``` **Form B — typed shortcodes** ```md - [ ] Ship datagrid v2 gh:anthropic/filemark#42 linear:ENG-1234 @alice !p0 ``` Expands to URLs via a built-in registry. Renders as icon-chip. Built-in shortcodes: | Prefix | Form | Expands to | |---|---|---| | `gh:org/repo#N` | PR | `https://github.com/org/repo/pull/N` (auto-detects issue vs PR) | | `gh:org/repo!N` | Issue (alt) | `https://github.com/org/repo/issues/N` | | `gh:org/repo@` | Commit | `https://github.com/org/repo/commit/` | | `gh:org/repo` | Repo | `https://github.com/org/repo` | | `gl:org/repo!N` | GitLab MR | per config | | `linear:TEAM-N` | Linear issue | per workspace config | | `jira:PROJ-N` | Jira issue | per domain config | | `slack:/` | Slack permalink | per workspace config | | `notion:` | Notion page | | | `figma:` | Figma file | | | `yt:` | YouTube | | Unknown prefix: rendered as literal text with a muted chip; no error. **Form C — URL pattern detection** Bare URLs in task text are classified against the registry: ```md - [ ] Ship datagrid v2 https://github.com/org/repo/pull/42 @alice ``` → detected as `github-pr`, rendered as the same icon-chip as `gh:org/repo#42`. **Form D — custom field namespace** For refs outside the registry: ```md - [ ] Ship v2 @alice x-pr=https://… x-design=https://figma.com/… ``` `x-=` — Layer 9 extension. Renders as generic chip unless a plugin registers a renderer for that field name. Custom shortcodes can also be registered at runtime: `tasks.registerShortcode("asana", (id) => `https://app.asana.com/0/${id}`)`. ### 4.6 Layer 6 — Relationships (dependency graph) Tasks form a DAG. Five relationship sigils, all using `:` as the typed-ref namespace marker. | Sigil | Meaning | Notes | |---|---|---| | `after:` | This task depends on `` being done. | Renders "blocked by" hint until prerequisite clears. | | `before:` | Inverse; this task blocks ``. | Usually written as `after:` on the other side. | | `blocks:` | Alias for `before:`. | Authoring preference. | | `requires:` | Strong dependency — unavailable until met. | Stricter than `after:`. | | `parent:` | Explicit parent link (beyond indentation). | Useful for cross-file parent/child relationships. | | `children:` | Explicit children list. | Inverse of `parent:`. | | `related:` | Soft link. | No blocking semantics. | Multiple ids comma-separated: `after:task-a,task-b`. Enables: Gantt rendering (critical path), "show me unblocked tasks" predicate, "finish this → these unblock" view. **v1.0 subset:** `after:` and `parent:` only. Full graph features (`requires:`, `blocks:`, `related:`) land in v1.1. ### 4.7 Layer 7 — Recurrence ✅ **shipped in Phase 5** Tasks that repeat on a schedule. Author sigil: `every:`. **Plain-English explainer (for humans + AI agents):** A recurrence token is a tag that says **"this task repeats."** That's it. Three things happen: 1. **Filemark renders a 🔁 chip** next to the task. A reader can see at a glance that it's routine, not a one-off. 2. **Filter predicates (`is:recurring`, `has:recurrence`) include it** in views that ask for routines. The same task can be excluded from a one-off backlog with `NOT is:recurring`. 3. **AI agents get an unambiguous machine-readable marker.** When the user asks "what's my weekly routine?" or "carry forward last week's routines," the agent greps `every:…` and knows exactly which bullets are periodic vs. which were one-shots. **What filemark does NOT do** — this is the important part. Filemark is a **reader**, not a scheduler. Marking a recurring task `[x]` does **not** auto-create the next instance. The markdown file stays exactly as the author wrote it. The `every:` tag is **informational**, not behavioral. **What happens when the next instance is due:** the user (or their AI) writes the next bullet. Because the tag is machine-readable, an AI can do this reliably: ``` User: "Copy last week's recurring routine to this Monday." AI: greps `every:` → lists matching rows → appends fresh bullets with today's ~due. User: reviews the diff, approves, done. ``` That's the intended workflow. It's **not** automation-for-its-own-sake. It's markdown-first + AI-assisted. **Supported forms (v1):** | Spec | Meaning | |---|---| | `every:daily` | every day | | `every:weekly` | every 7 days | | `every:biweekly` | every 14 days (alias for `every:2weeks`) | | `every:monthly` | every calendar month | | `every:quarterly` | every 3 months | | `every:yearly` / `every:annually` | every calendar year | | `every:mon,wed,fri` | specific weekdays (any subset of `sun..sat`) | | `every:2weeks` / `every:3weeks` | every N weeks | | `every:7d` / `every:10d` | every N days | | `every:first-monday` | first Monday of each month | | `every:last-friday` | last Friday of each month | Payload is parsed into a typed `Recurrence` object with a `kind` discriminator (`daily`, `weekly`, `biweekly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `yearly`, `custom-days`, `every-n-days`, `every-n-weeks`, `anchored`) plus the relevant sub-fields. Round-trip serializer preserves the original `display` string. **Analogy for users coming from other tools:** same concept as Google Calendar's "Repeats weekly" flag. Calendar shows a 🔁 icon + lets you view repeating events separately. The difference: Calendar auto-creates future instances in its own database; filemark keeps your markdown canonical and asks the AI (or you) to write the next instance explicitly. **Typical use cases:** - Personal routines: gym, journaling, weekly review - Work rhythms: standups, sprint planning, 1:1s, on-call handoff - Maintenance: rent, SSL rotation, backup verification, log archive - Commitments: quarterly goal review, annual performance, taxes ### 4.8 Layer 8 — Queries (predicate DSL) See §9 — documented as its own section because the view components (``, ``, ``) consume it heavily. ### 4.9 Layer 9 — Extensibility Three extension mechanisms keep the DSL future-proof: 1. **Custom fields — `x-=`.** Parser accepts, Task object gets `customFields["x-name"] = value`. Renderer shows generic chip unless a plugin registers a renderer. 2. **Grammar versioning — `tasks-version: 1.0`.** Frontmatter or fence info-string. Parser routes to the versioned grammar. Old docs keep rendering after grammar upgrades. 3. **Plugin renderers.** Chip renderer, link resolver, custom groupers, custom view components — all registered via a small plug-in surface in `@filemark/tasks`. --- ## 5. Parsing rules ### 5.1 The tail-scan rule Metadata is a **trailing tail** on the task line. Parser scans right-to-left, consuming valid sigil tokens until it hits a token that isn't a sigil. Everything before that boundary is verbatim text. ``` - [ ] Ship #grid v2 @alice !p0 ~2026-04-28 ↑─── text ──↑ ↑─ metadata ─↑ ``` `#grid` inside the text is preserved because it's not in the trailing block. Solves ~95% of sigil-in-prose collisions with zero author ceremony. ### 5.2 The `::` fence When text legitimately ends with a sigil-looking token, the author forces a metadata section: ```md - [ ] Email @channel about the #launch :: @alice !p1 ``` `::` separates text (left) from metadata (right). Sigils in text are literal. ### 5.3 Backslash escape ```md - [ ] Check \#grid tag @alice !p0 ``` `\#`, `\@`, `\!`, `\~`, `\^`, `\*` — parser strips the backslash and keeps the literal character in text. ### 5.4 Inline code is literal ```md - [ ] Review `#grid` tag @alice ``` `` `#grid` `` is an inline code AST node — untouchable by the task parser (which operates on text nodes only). Free literal escape. ### 5.5 Dense key-value block — `{k:v, k:v}` Alternate form when a task has lots of metadata and the author prefers explicit structure: ```md - [ ] Ship datagrid v2 {owner: alice, priority: p0, due: 2026-04-28, tags: [grid, v2], project: launch} ``` Inside `{…}`: comma-separated `key: value` pairs, YAML-subset syntax. Arrays use `[a, b, c]`. Same parser produces identical Task object as the sigil form. Author picks whichever is clearer per line. The `{…}` block must end the line (i.e., it takes the tail slot like sigils do). ### 5.6 Cascading defaults Each explicit value wins; missing values fall through this priority chain: ``` task line > fence info-string > frontmatter > filemark-global settings ``` Cascade at parse time, not query time. Six rules protect it; violations are rejected features. ### 6.1 One task = one line (the invariant) No line continuation. No multi-line YAML. No wrapped metadata. If a task needs more than one line, it splits into parent + indented child bullets, each a single line. ### 6.2 Sigils are single ASCII characters `@ ! ~ ^ # & $ % . * ( ) : +/- =` — each has exactly one meaning. No Unicode. No escaping of sigils in common case. ### 6.3 Token payloads are `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+` Identifier-safe. No quoted strings. No spaces in identifiers. Rich content lives in task text, not in metadata payloads. ### 6.4 Dates are ISO-canonical `~2026-04-28` or a small set of keywords. No locale-specific date formats. Regex: `~(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}|today|tomorrow|yesterday|e[odwmqy]|this-week|next-week|\+\d+[dwmy])`. ### 6.5 Status char lives at a fixed column offset After `bullet SP`, always `[X]` where X is one of 6 chars. Regex `^\s*[-*+] \[[\sx/!?-]\] ` matches every task line with zero false positives. ### 6.6 Metadata tokens are space-delimited Always: `@alice !p0 ~fri #grid`. Never `@alice!p0~fri#grid`. `\s+` works as the separator. Formatter normalizes tab → single space. ### 6.7 Grep patterns that work today ```bash # every task grep -En '^\s*[-*+] \[[ x/!?-]\] ' FILE # open only (todo or wip) grep -En '^\s*[-*+] \[[ /]\] ' FILE # done grep -En '^\s*[-*+] \[x\] ' FILE # alice's tasks grep -En '^\s*[-*+] \[.\].*\s@alice(\s|$)' FILE # p0 anywhere grep -En '!p0(\s|$)' FILE # due today grep -En '~today(\s|$)' FILE # due in a specific week grep -En '~2026-04-(2[4-9]|30)\b' FILE # github PR links (any form) grep -En '\b(gh:[A-Za-z0-9._-]+/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+#\d+|github\.com/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+/pull/\d+)' FILE # stable-id references grep -En '\^task-ship-datagrid\b' FILE # all task fences grep -En '^```tasks\b' FILE # by project grep -En '\(launch\)(\s|$)' FILE # by area grep -En '\.area/work\b' FILE # tasks with an estimate grep -En '\s&[0-9]+[mhdw]\b' FILE ``` Every pattern is a one-liner. No AST, no parser call, no language server. That's the test. ### 6.8 Rejected features (and why) | Rejected | Why | |---|---| | Multi-line YAML metadata per task | Breaks one-line invariant | | Quoted string values (`@"alice smith"`) | Word-boundary regex breaks | | Unicode sigils (✓ ⏰ 🔥) | Cross-platform regex issues | | JSON-in-line full-object syntax | `{k:v}` sigil form is denser + greppable | | Sigils concatenated (`@alice!p0`) | Breaks `\s+` delimiter | | Nested sigils (`@alice{since:yesterday}`) | Breaks single-token rule | | Negation inside a task line (`!!p0`) | Ambiguous; negation is query-level, not task-level | Each rejection buys grep-friendliness. Each design choice that reads as human-friendly is also AI-friendly, for the same reasons: low ambiguity, positional rules, round-trip guarantees. ### 11.1 Round-trip guarantee `parse(line) → serialize(task)` is byte-identical for canonical inputs. Non-canonical inputs (metadata in unusual order) normalize to canonical on re-serialize. Enables AI edits: ``` 1. read line → Task 2. modify single field in Task 3. serializeTask(task) → new line 4. replace source line in file ``` No whole-file AST surgery. No accidental clobber of comments, formatting, or unrelated tokens. ### 11.2 Simple positional rules "Put metadata at the end; stop when you want." One sentence. LLMs emit correct syntax first try. ### 11.3 Non-overlapping ASCII sigils `@ ! ~ ^ # & $ % . * ( ) :` — each has exactly one meaning. No precedence rules, no operator overloading. Models pattern-match instantly. ### 11.4 Typed shortcodes are prefix-namespaced `gh:` / `linear:` / `jira:` — self-describing. Adding a new shortcode is a registry entry; the model learns via example in the system prompt. ### 11.5 Natural-language → structured pipeline User: *"Alice ships datagrid by Friday, high prio, PR at github.com/org/repo/pull/42."* Single LLM pass: ```md - [ ] Ship datagrid @alice !p0 ~fri gh:org/repo#42 ``` Every token maps 1:1 to the description. No structured-output prompt engineering. ### 11.6 Diagnostics enable self-correction `"Unknown priority '!veryhigh' at sprint-2.md:14 — did you mean !p0?"` — an AI tool-use loop reads the diagnostic, fixes the value, resubmits. DSL self-teaches in a tool-use context. ### 11.7 Cascade = shorter AI output Frontmatter `default-owner: alice` means every task line is shorter. AI plans often have 20+ tasks with same owner/project; cascade cuts token count in half. Context stays small; latency stays low. ### 11.8 Predicate DSL as NL-translation target LLM translates "show me overdue p0 tasks assigned to grace with open PRs" → `is:overdue AND priority=p0 AND owner=grace AND has:pr`. Predicate grammar is simple enough to be a reliable structured-output target. ### 11.9 AI action markers First-class integration points for AI-driven enrichment: ```md - [ ] Research competitor pricing @ai:summarize-findings - [ ] Write launch email @ai:draft-from-tasks - [ ] Review PR @ai:summarize-diff gh:org/repo#42 ``` `@ai:` sigil renders a ✨ button. Click → AI call (via configured API key) runs the action with task + linked refs as context, appends a child bullet with findings. ### 11.10 Bulk-edit safety "Bump every p1 task in sprint-2.md by a week": 1. `filterTasks(allTasks, "priority=p1 AND file=sprint-2.md")` → 7 matches 2. For each: `task.due = addWeeks(task.due, 1)` → `serializeTask()` → replace line 3. Round-trip guarantee means untouched tokens are byte-preserved 4. Diff is clean: 7 lines changed, dates +7 days ### 11.11 The AI agent loop (grep-first workflow) Typical tool-use loop against a filemark repo. Every step uses standard Unix tools or `filemark tasks` CLI — no parser instantiation inside the model. ``` 1. User: "Which overdue p0 tasks does grace own across all opened docs?" 2. AI tool call: bash "grep -Enr '!p0' ~/notes | grep '@grace' | grep -Ev '\[x\]|\[-\]'" 3. Response (file:line:content per match, deterministic format): ~/notes/sprint-2.md:14:- [ ] Ship datagrid v2 @grace !p0 ~2026-04-20 #grid ~/notes/infra.md:37:- [!] DB migration blocked @grace !p0 #infra 4. For each hit, AI grep-extracts ~due with one regex pass: match.groups.due = /~(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})/ if due < today → overdue 5. For structured fields AI needs beyond grep (links, dependencies): filemark tasks show sprint-2.md:14 → returns the serialized Task object as JSON 6. AI makes edit decisions — e.g. bump priority, reassign owner: read single line parseTaskLine(line) → Task modify field serializeTask(task) → new line write back single line 7. No whole-file AST manipulation. No context pollution with unrelated doc content. Edits are surgical and diff-clean. ``` **Net:** AI only loads the lines it needs. Context stays small. Latency stays low. Round-trip guarantee means programmatic edits never clobber formatting. ### 11.12 Natural-language → DSL translation The predicate DSL is a reliable structured-output target: ``` User: "show me overdue p0 tasks assigned to grace with open PRs" LLM emits: is:overdue AND priority=p0 AND owner=grace AND has:pr Tool call: filemark tasks grep "is:overdue AND priority=p0 AND owner=grace AND has:pr" Response: deterministic file:line:content list ``` Same pattern for creation: ``` User: "Alice needs to ship datagrid by Friday, high priority, PR already open at github.com/org/repo/pull/42" LLM emits: - [ ] Ship datagrid @alice !p0 ~fri gh:org/repo#42 Tool call: append the line to the active sprint doc ``` Every token in the emitted markdown maps 1:1 from the natural-language description. ### 11.13 Bumper-sticker summary **World-class DSL = one task per line, ASCII sigils, ISO dates, space-delimited tokens, identifier-safe payloads, canonical formatter.** Everything else in the grammar — richness, typed refs, shortcodes, predicates, dependencies, recurrence — layers on top of those six invariants without breaking them. Grep remains the universal solvent; round-trip parse/serialize remains byte-identical; AI emits correctly on first try and edits surgically. ### 11.14 What lifts it from "great DSL" to "world-class DSL" Each of these is a design choice we've committed to in the grammar: - **Typed everything** — priority, date, duration, money, percent are first-class types, not strings - **Predictable parser** — tail-scan + escape hatches + cascade; no ambiguity, no hidden context - **Expressive without ceremony** — simple case is one bullet; advanced case is the same bullet with a `{…}` tail or fence flags - **Programmable at every layer** — query DSL, view composition, grouping, sorting, custom fields, custom chip renderers - **Self-documenting diagnostics** — warnings tell you what's wrong and where - **Interop-first** — exports to every common task format; imports from the big three - **Round-trip guarantee** — parse/serialize is reversible; AI-driven edits never clobber formatting - **Plug-in extensible** — custom fields, custom chip renderers, custom view components, custom predicates - **Grammar-versioned** — docs aren't held hostage to future parser changes - **Formal grammar shipped** — third parties can build on it without guessing - **Grep-friendly by invariant** — six rules make bash+regex a first-class query path --- ## 12. Task details — rich body content (Phase 5.5, 2026-04-24) A task can have arbitrary **rich detail** underneath its one-line bullet: paragraphs, images, code fences, tables, callouts, and full filemark components (Chart, Kanban, Stats, ADR, TaskList, TaskTimeline — anything). The detail is authored as standard indented markdown under the bullet and renders in a **popup sheet** (right-side drawer), not inline. Nested tasks can also have their own details. This preserves the three core invariants: - **One task = one line** (grep still works; detail is collected via follow-up indented blocks) - **Markdown is source of truth** (no new grammar — just GFM loose-list indentation) - **Reader-first** (filemark never writes back) ### 18b.1 Authoring Indent block-level content at least one column past the bullet marker: ```md - [ ] Ship datagrid v2 @alice !p0 ~2026-04-30 #grid Virtualization lets us handle 100K+ rows at 60fps. ![mockup](./mocks/datagrid-v2.png) ```ts interface VirtualizationOpts { rowHeight: number; } ``` | Approach | Memory | Complexity | |---|---|---| | Fixed | O(n) | low | | Estimator | O(n log n) | medium | **Subtasks:** - [x] Audit current perf @alice - [/] Sketch virtualization API @alice Richer subtask detail — yes, subtasks can have their own popups too. Each gets its own sheet. - [ ] Next task ``` Any GFM-parsable content (paragraphs, fenced code, images, tables, blockquotes, HTML / MDX tags) is valid. Filemark's component tags (``, ``, ``, ``, ``, nested ``) all work inside a detail because the sheet renders through the same `@filemark/mdx` `` pipeline. ### 18b.2 The Task.detail field ```ts interface Task { // …existing fields… /** Raw markdown source slice of all block-level content indented * beneath the bullet (excluding nested task-bullets, which become * subTasks). Common indent is stripped so the source is re-rendered * from its natural left margin. */ detail?: string; /** 1-based line range [startLine, endLine] of the detail in the * original source. Enables the sheet to open the right region of * the doc when the user clicks "edit source". */ detailLineRange?: [number, number]; } ``` `detail` is **always a string** (not an mdast array) for portability and round-trip simplicity. Rendering is delegated to the same react-markdown pipeline the host uses — the sheet reads the host's components map from a new `MDXComponentsContext` (see §8). ### 18b.3 Parser — line-based detail collection extractTasks walks each task bullet and scans forward until the task's scope ends. Inside the scope, it separates: - **Nested task bullets** (`- [ ] ...` at indent ≥ content column) → `subTasks` - **Non-task bullets** (`- foo` at indent ≥ content column) → `notes` (current behavior; retained for small breadcrumbs) - **Everything else** — paragraphs, fenced code (generic ``` or ~~~), images, tables, HTML / MDX tags, callouts — → `detail` (raw source, common-indent-stripped) Generic code-fence state tracking prevents false positives (e.g., a line starting with `-` inside a code fence isn't a bullet). ### 18b.4 Rendering — popup sheet A new `` component lives in `@filemark/mdx`: - **Portal-based**: renders into `document.body` via `ReactDOM.createPortal` so the sheet isn't clipped by any parent overflow / transform. - **Right-side drawer**: slides in from the right (animation ~200ms), ~560px wide on desktop, full-width on narrow viewports. - **Backdrop**: semi-transparent overlay behind the sheet; click closes. - **Close affordances**: `X` button in header, Escape key, backdrop click. - **Header**: task status glyph + text + chips (mirrors the inline row). - **Body**: scrollable; renders `task.detail` through the host's `components` map pulled from `MDXComponentsContext` — so Chart / Kanban / Stats / nested TaskList all work. - **Footer**: optional "edit source" link that jumps the viewer to `detailLineRange[0]` (uses the existing `scrollTarget` flow from Phase 4). ### 18b.5 Affordance on the task row In the inline `` and in `` / `` / `` cards, tasks with `detail` show a small **📎 N** (or **▸ detail**) chip. Click opens the sheet. Hovering the chip shows a preview tooltip with the first 80 chars of the detail. ### 18b.6 Nested task detail Since subtasks are themselves `Task` entries in the flat array (just with `depth > 0` and `parentId` set), each subtask has its own `detail` field. Rendering a subtask in the list shows its own chevron if it has a detail; opens its own sheet independently. ### 18b.7 New MDXComponentsContext The sheet needs the host's `components` map (Chart / Kanban / Stats / etc.). Pulling it through props from every surface is awkward; instead a small new React context: ```ts // @filemark/mdx/src/components-context.tsx export const MDXComponentsContext = createContext(null); export function useMDXComponents(): ComponentsMap | null { return useContext(MDXComponentsContext); } ``` MDXViewer wraps its children in `` so any descendant (including portal-rendered sheets) can read the same map. ### 18b.8 New CSS tokens Add to `packages/mdx-viewer/src/styles.css`: | Variable | Fallback | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `--fm-task-sheet-width` | `min(560px, 100%)` | drawer width | | `--fm-task-sheet-bg` | `var(--background)` | drawer bg | | `--fm-task-sheet-border` | `1px solid var(--border)` | drawer border | | `--fm-task-sheet-backdrop` | `rgba(0,0,0,0.4)` | backdrop color | | `--fm-task-sheet-animation-duration` | `200ms` | slide-in duration | | `--fm-task-sheet-padding` | `20px 24px` | body padding | | `--fm-task-sheet-z` | `1000` | z-index | Catalog these in `docsi/THEMING.md §6` as a new family. ### 18b.9 Non-goals (for v1) - **Multiple simultaneously-open sheets.** One sheet at a time; clicking another task's detail swaps the current one. - **Resizing the drawer.** Width is token-driven; fixed per theme. - **"Full screen" mode.** Could be added later (expand the drawer to fill the viewport); skip for v1. - **Inline expansion fallback.** Per user feedback, inline would disrupt doc scannability — drawer only. --- ## 19. Authoring caveats (surfaced during Phase 1–5 build) These are real issues that showed up when authoring the demo doc + rendering in playground. None are parser bugs — they're properties of the HTML/markdown substrate filemark uses. Future docs (and AIs writing those docs) need to know them. ### 19.1 Custom-tag self-close is a lie in HTML5 `` looks self-closing but HTML5 parses it as `` (open, no close). Everything after the tag becomes its children — which our component ignores, so *nothing after it visually renders*. **Rule:** always use explicit open/close pairs for custom components embedded in markdown: ```md ``` Void HTML elements like `
    ` / `` can self-close because they're in the HTML5 spec. Custom elements (anything not in the spec) cannot. ### 19.2 `<` in an HTML attribute value breaks the tag parser `` — the `<=` chars look fine inside quotes but many HTML parsers (including rehype-raw's parse5 backend) eat everything from `<` onward as a new nested tag. The result: the whole attribute value is lost and everything after gets mis-parented. **Rule:** avoid `<` and `>` in HTML-attribute filter values. Use the set form or the derived predicates: | Don't write | Write instead | |---|---| | `filter="priority<=p1"` | `filter="priority in (p0,p1)"` | | `filter="due<=today"` | `filter="is:overdue OR is:today"` | | `filter="due<=eow"` | `filter="is:overdue OR is:today OR is:upcoming"` | | `filter="estimate>2h"` | use `>` entity, or put the predicate in a `` ```tasks `` fence | Inside a `` ```tasks `` code fence, predicates with `<` are fine — the fence isn't HTML-parsed. This only affects HTML-tag attribute values. ### 19.3 CSS lives in two places — chrome-ext and playground New `.fv-*` classes (chip colors, table options, download menus) need to be added to BOTH: - `apps/chrome-ext/src/styles/index.css` — the extension body - `apps/playground/src/styles.css` — the playground dev surface Both files intentionally duplicate the `.fv-mdx-body` block (the playground can't import from the extension app). When adding new `.fv-*` classes, add to both. Future improvement: extract a shared `@filemark/styles` package so both hosts import the same source. Not done yet. ### 19.4 The `md` presence flag `` and `` use `md` as a presence-only attribute (no value). HTML sends it through as `md=""`. Our detection uses `"md" in p` — empty-string still satisfies the key check. Tested and works. If you need to force this off for any reason, write `md="false"` — but `"false"` is still truthy-looking so it still routes to the task-source path. Future fix: change detection to `p.md !== "false"` if we ever need an opt-out. ### 19.5 Task text that starts with `@` / `!` / `#` etc. Tail-scan means metadata lives at the END of the line, so a sentence starting with a sigil is fine — `@channel heads up` parses `@channel` as an owner (last token in a one-token tail — problem), unless there's trailing metadata that claims the tail first. **Rule:** put metadata at the end. If your task text legitimately has a sigil-looking token at the end, use the `::` fence: ```md - [ ] Remember to ping @team :: @alice !p1 ``` Or backslash-escape: ```md - [ ] Remember to ping \@team @alice !p1 ``` ### 19.6 Sections 18+ disappeared during Phase 2/3 QA Happened during the very first render of `examples/tasks-full.md`. Root cause: self-close quirk (§19.1) — `` at §17 ate §18–§25 as children. Fixed by switching every custom tag to explicit close form. Kept as a known-pattern here for future AI sessions writing demo docs. ### 19.7 Phase 4 — CSS chip rules needed to escape `.fv-mdx-body` scope The TaskPanel renders outside the `.fv-mdx-body` root (it's in the app shell, not inside a rendered doc). The chip rules originally lived scoped under `.fv-mdx-body .fv-task-chip*`, so the panel rendered unstyled chips on first build. Fix: unscoped the chip rules to just `.fv-task-chip*` in both `apps/chrome-ext/src/styles/index.css` and `apps/playground/src/styles.css`. This is a general lesson — any CSS for task rendering must work both inside a rendered markdown doc AND in app-shell surfaces (panel, search results, sidebar row hover previews). ### 19.8 Phase 4 — chrome-ext needed the `@filemark/tasks` dependency added explicitly The `apps/chrome-ext/package.json` didn't list `@filemark/tasks` — it worked transitively through `@filemark/mdx`, but `import { extractTasks } from "@filemark/tasks"` in the shell app couldn't resolve the type declarations. Lesson: when a chrome-ext-only file imports from a workspace package, add it to `chrome-ext/package.json` directly; don't rely on transitive resolution from mdx-viewer. ### 19.9 Phase 4 — `⌘T` browser shortcut reminder `Cmd/Ctrl + T` opens a new tab in a normal browser context, but chrome-extension:// pages don't inherit that binding — we own the whole keydown surface. Safe to bind. If we ever move to a regular website surface (e.g. filemark.app), we'd need to pick a different shortcut or scope via a conditional check. --- ## 20.
